explanation:
[EFFECT] Temperature has a strongly non-monotonic, arc-shaped effect: near-freezing conditions (normalised temp ≈ 0, about 0 °C) heavily suppress demand (contribution near −0.9), rising temperatures sharply increase the contribution up to a peak around a normalised value of 0.6 (roughly 25 °C, contribution ~+0.25), and then the contribution declines modestly at very high temperatures. The effect is asymmetric — the cold penalty is much steeper than the hot-weather decline.
[IMPORTANCE] This is a high-importance feature, with a total vertical range of roughly 1.1 log-units, ranking among the top three or four features.
[RECOMMENDATION] Plan your staffing and bike availability primarily around the hour of the day — the evening peak (around 5–6 pm) and the morning shoulder (around 8 am) drive the largest swings in demand — and use temperature as the key weather signal, targeting comfortable mild days (~20–25 °C) for maximum expected ridership and scaling back during cold or very hot spells.
